stemMarkdown: Two runners start together from the same point on a circular track 400 m long and run in the same direction at 10 km/h and 6 km/h. After how many seconds does the faster runner first lap the slower one? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: In the same direction the speeds subtract: $1.1111$ m/s. To meet again the faster runner must gain a full lap of 400 m, which takes $\dfrac{400}{1.1111} = 360.0$ seconds.
altSolutionMarkdown: Meeting on a circle means the gap between them has grown to exactly one whole lap.
